# Resource: stripe_billing_meter

Defines how usage events are aggregated into a billable quantity. `terraform destroy` deactivates the meter, because Stripe cannot delete one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_billing_meter" "api_calls" {
  display_name = "API calls"
  event_name   = "api_call"

  default_aggregation = {
    formula = "sum"
  }

  customer_mapping = {
    type              = "by_id"
    event_payload_key = "stripe_customer_id"
  }

  value_settings = {
    event_payload_key = "value"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `default_aggregation` - (Required) The default settings to aggregate a meter's events with. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`default_aggregation`](#default_aggregation) below.
* `display_name` - (Required) The meter’s name. Not visible to the customer.
* `event_name` - (Required) The name of the meter event to record usage for. Corresponds with the `event_name` field on meter events. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `customer_mapping` - (Optional) Fields that specify how to map a meter event to a customer. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`customer_mapping`](#customer_mapping) below.
* `event_time_window` - (Optional) The time window which meter events have been pre-aggregated for, if any. Possible values: `day`, `hour`. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `value_settings` - (Optional) Fields that specify how to calculate a meter event's value. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`value_settings`](#value_settings) below.

<a id="customer_mapping"></a>
### `customer_mapping`

The `customer_mapping` attribute supports:

* `event_payload_key` - (Required) The key in the meter event payload to use for mapping the event to a customer.
* `type` - (Required) The method for mapping a meter event to a customer. Possible values: `by_id`.

<a id="default_aggregation"></a>
### `default_aggregation`

The `default_aggregation` attribute supports:

* `formula` - (Required) Specifies how events are aggregated. Possible values: `count`, `last`, `sum`.

<a id="value_settings"></a>
### `value_settings`

The `value_settings` attribute supports:

* `event_payload_key` - (Required) The key in the meter event payload to use as the value for this meter.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `status` - The meter's status. Possible values: `active`, `inactive`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.
* `updated` - Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `deactivated_at` - The time the meter was deactivated, if any. Measured in seconds since Unix epoch.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a billing meter using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_billing_meter.api_calls
  id = "mtr_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_billing_meter.api_calls
  identity = {
    id = "mtr_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the billing meter.

Using `terraform import`, import a billing meter using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_billing_meter.api_calls mtr_123
```
